title: Oh God! Thy Name They Well May Praise
description: Oh God! Thy Name They Well May Praise in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Felicia Hemans wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 827 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"These see the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Oh God! thy name they well may praise, Who to the deep go down, And trace the won-ders of thy ways, Where rocks and bil-lows frown.

lines: Oh God! thy name they well may praise,
Who to the deep go down,
And trace the wonders of thy ways,
For many a fair majestic sight
If glorious be that awful deep,
What then art thou, who bid'st it keep
Let heaven and earth in praise unite,
Whose word can rouse the tempest's might,

licence: Public domain: Felicia Hemans died in 1835.
credits: Words by Felicia Hemans (1793–1835), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
